evidence.quoted_text:
def acquire(self):
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        try:
            descriptor = os.open(self.path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL
                                 | os.O_WRONLY, 0o600)
        except FileExistsError as exc:
            raise Refused(
                "admission is already held by " + str(self.path)
                + "; another deploy or a manual hold owns it") from exc
        # From here the marker exists even if the token never lands.
        self.created = True
        try:
            with os.fdopen(descriptor, "wb") as handle:
                handle.write(self.token)
                handle.flush()
                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
evidence.reason: The current Hold.acquire creates the admission marker with O_CREAT|O_EXCL and fsyncs only the token file descriptor at line 412; it never opens or fsyncs self.path.parent after creating the directory entry. The same durability issue applies to removal in release(), which unlinks the marker without a parent-directory fsync. As a result, a power loss can lose the marker directory entry even though the token file was synced, leaving no durable admission hold; an unsynced removal can likewise leave a stale hold. This is an implementation defect in the existing admission-hold behavior, not a proposal to add a new requirement.
